topicConditionsHtml:
General conditions

Applicants are invited to carefully read all the provisions below before preparing and submitting their proposals.

 

The topic is described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022..

 

The estimated EU budget for this topic is given in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022 and in the topic header above. For the most up to date information concerning the budget commitments of the KDT JU Participating States applicants are invited to check the KDT JU web site: https://www.kdt-ju.europa.eu/calls/kdt-ju-calls-2022

More information for the Swiss applicants interested to participate in KDT Calls 2022 (RIA and IA Actions) is available here:  International tenders (innosuisse.ch)

The specific provisions and funding rates (both EU and national) are described in the KDT-JU Work Programme 2022.

 

The complex funding rates of KDT JU IA call 2022 and the limitations of the submission system resulted in the fact that the funding rates of the large enterprises (for profit not SMEs) are not adequately integrated in the JU/EU Budget table in the Part A. Consequently, these organizations need to calculate their JU/EU Funding as instructed in the Guide for Applicants (examples for each Call/topic are presented).

Similarly, the National Budgets/Funding Table are not anymore integrated into the Part A (as it was the case in the past for the ECSEL JU) and it needs to be uploaded as a separate xls file in the dedicated place holder in the submission tool. More details/instructions are provided in the Guide for Applicants

The Part C are now named National Part in the submission tool to avoid confusion with the Part C (dynamic forms) used by other programmes. More details are provided in the Guide for Applicants

 

General conditions

Admissibility conditions: are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Proposal page limits and layout are described in Part B of the Proposal Template available in the Submission System

The page limit of the application is as follows:

  • The page limit for the chapter on EXCELLENCE is 60 pages
  • The page limit for the chapter on IMPACT is 100 pages
  • The page limit for the chapter on IMPLEMENTATION is 100 pages.

 

 

 

Eligible countries: described in Annex 1 (EU funding) and Annex 4 (National/Regional funding) of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Eligibility conditions: described in Annex 1, Call/Topic Description and Annex 4 (specific National/ Regional Funding eligibility conditions) of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

 

Financial and operational capacity and exclusion: described in Annex 1 of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022 and Annex C of the Work Programme General Annexes

 

Evaluation criteria, scoring and thresholds are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

The following additions to the general award criteria apply:

  1. The scores will be given with a resolution of one decimal
  2. The overall threshold, applying to the sum of the three individual scores, will be 11
  3. To determine the ranking the score for ‘Impact’ will be given a weight of 1.5 and the score for "Implementation" will be given a weight of 0.7

Submission and evaluation processes are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022, the KDT PAB Decision on evaluation, and selection procedures, and the Online Manual

Indicative timeline for evaluation and grant agreement: described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Grants awarded under this topic will be linked to the other actions selected under ‘RISC-V’ topics in this call, previous, and future calls. Respective options under Article 3 and Article 7 of the Model Grant Agreement will be used to this end.

 Legal and financial set-up of the grants: described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

 

Specific conditions

All the conditions are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

In this Call the integration of the gender dimension (sex and gender analysis) in research and innovation content is not a mandatory requirement. However, proposals with activities concerning the user interaction or sensing (e.g. medical devices, consumer goods, cars with automatic driving features, ...) need to include (if relevant) considerations of how the gender dimension affects system design, and hence whether it affects the technical specifications.

 

Selected actions will be implemented as ‘linked actions’, i.e. they are linked with other actions selected under ‘RISC-V’ topics in this call and future calls. Respective options under Article 3 and Article 7 of the Model Grant Agreement will be used to this end.

 

Members of consortium are required to conclude a consortium agreement, in principle prior to the signature of the grant agreement.

Call/Topic Documents:

KDT JU Work Programme 2022

ECS-SRIA-2022

Essential Information for Clinical Studies (only for proposals including clinical studies)

Template Model National Budgets Table  (this is only a model for applicants information; the template to be used for submission is available in the Submission System)

topicConditionsHtml:
General conditions

Applicants are invited to carefully read all the provisions below before preparing and submitting their proposals.

 

The "Grand Challenges" opened in this topic are listed in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022 and described in detail in the ECS SRIA 2022.

 

The estimated EU budget for this topic is given in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022 and in the topic header above. For the most up to date information concerning the budget commitments of the KDT JU Participating States applicants are invited to check the KDT JU web site: https://www.kdt-ju.europa.eu/calls/kdt-ju-calls-2022

 More information for the Swiss applicants interested to participate in KDT Calls 2022 (RIA and IA Actions) is available here:  International tenders (innosuisse.ch)

The specific provisions and funding rates (both EU and national) are described in the KDT-JU Work Programme 2022.

 

The complex funding rates of KDT JU RIA call 2022 and the limitations of the submission system resulted in the fact that the funding rates of the large enterprises (for profit not SMEs) are not adequately integrated in the JU/EU Budget table in the Part A. Consequently, these organizations need to calculate their JU/EU Funding as instructed in the Guide for Applicants (examples for each Call/topic are presented).

Similarly, the National Budgets/Funding Table are not anymore integrated into the Part A (as it was the case in the past for the ECSEL JU) and it needs to be uploaded as a separate xls file in the dedicated place holder in the submission tool. More details/instructions are provided in the Guide for Applicants

The Part C are now named National Part in the submission tool to avoid confusion with the Part C (dynamic forms) used by other programmes. More details are provided in the Guide for Applicants

 

General conditions

Admissibility conditions: are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Proposal page limits and layout: described in Part B of the Application Form available in the Submission System

The page limit of the application is as follows:

  • The page limit for the chapter on EXCELLENCE is 60 pages
  • The page limit for the chapter on IMPACT is 100 pages
  • The page limit for the chapter on IMPLEMENTATION is 100 pages.

 

 

Eligible countries: described in Annex 1 (EU funding) and Annex 4 (National/Regional funding) of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Eligibility conditions: described in Annex 1, Call/Topic Description and Annex 4 (specific National/ Regional Funding eligibility conditions) of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

The following additional eligibility criteria apply:

  • Consortium size limit: the maximum size is 50 participants.
  • Maximum EU contribution per project: the EU contribution per project is capped at 12M€
  • Maximum EU contribution per participant in a project is limited to 40% of the total EU funding for the project.

 

 

 

Financial and operational capacity and exclusion: described in Annex 1 of the KDT JU Work Programme 2022 and Annex C of the Work Programme General Annexes

 

Evaluation criteria, scoring and thresholds are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

The following additions to the general award criteria apply:

  1. The scores will be given with a resolution of one decimal
  2. The overall threshold, applying to the sum of the three individual scores, will be 11
  3. To determine the ranking the score for "Implementation" will be given a weight of 0.7

 

Submission and evaluation processes are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022, the KDT PAB Decision on evaluation, and selection procedures, and the Online Manual

Indicative timeline for evaluation and grant agreement: described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022

 

Legal and financial set-up of the grants: described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

 

All the conditions are described in the KDT JU Work Programme 2022.

 

In this Call the integration of the gender dimension (sex and gender analysis) in research and innovation content is not a mandatory requirement. However, proposals with activities concerning the user interaction or sensing (e.g. medical devices, consumer goods, cars with automatic driving features, ...) need to include (if relevant) considerations of how the gender dimension affects system design, and hence whether it affects the technical specifications.

 

Members of consortium are required to conclude a consortium agreement, in principle prior to the signature of the grant agreement.

title: Focus topic 6G Integrated Radio Front-End for TeraHertz Communications (IA)
description: Expected Outcome: THz communications emerge as a strong contender for 6G communication for a number of high-capacity applications, such as cellular backhaul, direct connection in industrial environments, and joint communication and sensing. Sub-THz applications (starting at 100 GHz up to 300 GHz) however open a range of issues and notably: i) very large number of antennas to co-integrate compared to mmWave implementation; ii) low PA power output; iii) limitation due to constant envelope of operations; iv) integration of heterogeneous technologies for antennas and for beamformers (e.g. BiCMOS and InP for front-ends, CMOS for other functionalities). In addition, different antenna architectures are being considered. Scope: Detailed descriptions can be found in the ECS SRIA2023. Aspects of ECS value chain integration are important for the KDT programme and the whole European ECS sector, across applications and across capabilities. Consortia are encouraged to submit proposals that take this aspect into account. Proposals that cut across disciplines, support platform building, interoperability, establishment of open standards are particularly encouraged; even outside the regular ECS sector. Proposals shall encourage SMEs to participate in the developments, in particular paying attention to the needs of SMEs, involve SMEs in project execution, and develop solutions that can be taken up and/or exploited by SMEs Proposals shall attempt to establish links with other projects and consortia from the Horizon Europe family (within cluster 4 or in other clusters) working on topics related to the proposal. Note that National priorities may be applicable to specific topics (refer to Annex 4 “COUNTRY SPECIFIC ELIGIBILITY RULES” ).
